newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan Muslim Commercial seen good buy.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan Muslim Commercial seen good buy.

text.p: Pakistan's private Muslim Commercial Bank Ltd is seen as having the best long-term potential among the listed commercial banks and leading brokerage houses have advised investors to buy the stock.

"There is a potential upside (to the current price) of almost 100 percent to the 60 rupees ($1.48) ($1.47) levels over the the next three years," SocGen-Crosby Securities said in a report received by Reuters on Wednesday.
MCB'S 10-rupee stock last closed 2.05 rupees up at 38.90 on the Karachi Stock Exchange.
Brokers said the new surge in the stock price was backed by an MCB statement on Tuesday that it has decided to cut interest charged on loans to customers by 1.09 percent from July 1.
Lending rates for the corporate sector averaged around 17.5 percent but most industrial and commercial borrowers were paying rates from 20 to 22 percent.
MCB said a central bank scheme for recovery of loans had helped it recover 550 million rupees and that a total of 1.5 billion rupees were likely to be recovered in 1997.
SocGen-Crosby said it had raised MCB's earnings forecast for 1997 by 31 percent, for 1998 by eight percent, and for 1999 by 13 percent.
ING Baring Securities, in a research note issued on Wednesday, said it was upgrading earnings forecast for MCB by 45 percent and 54 percent for 1997 and 1998 respectively.

MCB, the first state-run bank to be privatised in 1991, announced in March 1997 an after-tax profit of 103 million rupees for the year ending December 31, 1996, against a year-ago post-tax profit of 370 million rupees.
However, Crosby said top management changes at MCB had resulted in a shift in the bank's stategic focus from an agressive balance-sheet growth to prudent lending.

"While balance sheet growth was phenomenal in the post-privatisation years, earnings remained lacklustre campared to other private sector competitors because of higher (bad debt) provisioning levels," the report said.
It said the bank's current emphasis was on raising earnings enhancement by proper utilisation of resources while rationalising the cost structure.

"The bank's earlier aggressive lending policies have been abandoned in favour of prudent risk management, which should lower its provisioning as a percentage of advances." ($ = 40.41 Pakistani Rupees)
